## W9 feasibility blocker (2026-10-17)

**Hypothesis:** the existing `install-ctl` already has an interactive TUI selection surface that can be driven with `ratatui-testlib`, while scripted and interactive runs share an artifact-selection/install path.

**Falsifying checks performed:**

- `install/install-ctl/src/main.rs` defines only Clap commands (`install`, `uninstall`, `self-uninstall`, `update`, `catalog`, `start`, `prepare`, `viewer`, `guidance`, `workspace`) and dispatches `install <selection>` directly through `resolve_selection`; it defines no interactive command or terminal event/render loop.
- `install/install-ctl/Cargo.toml` has no `ratatui`, `ratatui-testlib`, `crossterm`, or comparable TUI dependency (including dev-dependencies).
- The W8-owned `.agents/skills/workflow-skill/SKILL.md` explicitly says the three bootstrap scripts are independently invokable and “there is no interactive selection step wiring them together yet”.
- The frozen ticket design/examples parts are empty, so they do not define the required selection screens, defaults, navigation/confirmation behavior, installation-home input, or the mapping from the requested categories “tools, agent client tools, instructions, hooks” to current `artifacts.toml` categories (`cli`, `mcp`, `misc`, `service`, `hook`).

The requested literal ratatui-testlib acceptance test cannot be truthfully added as a narrow integration: its system-under-test and selected artifact mapping are not designed in the approved ticket. `install-ctl/Cargo.toml` is also already dirty with unrelated, unstaged user work, so a dependency edit cannot be scoped/staged without mixing that work.

**Result:** no source, skill, or manifest files were changed; no proxy/unit-only substitute was run. A design amendment must specify the interactive flow and category/selection mapping (or revise the acceptance contract to a non-TUI path), and a clean ownership boundary for `install-ctl/Cargo.toml` is required before implementation. No W10 work was performed.

## W10 validation attempt

Retry justification: the catalog blocker was repaired in workflow-tools commit dcd87b7 before this retry.

`cargo check --manifest-path workflow-tools\install\install-ctl\Cargo.toml` exited 0 after the target-root/terminal-guard implementation, with existing workspace warnings only.

Focused literal test attempt: `cargo test --manifest-path workflow-tools\install\install-ctl\Cargo.toml --test tui_cancel -- --nocapture`. First attempt failed to compile because `portable_pty::CommandBuilder::env` rejects `Cow<str>` (E0277); repaired locally by passing `&Path`. One retry ran for 420 seconds without terminal output and was stopped; no pass/fail evidence was produced. Log pointer: `$HOME/AppData/Local/rtk/tee/1792241382_cargo_test.log` for the first failure; retry shell id 2550.

The earlier full manifest command remains the exact failed test `guidance::tests::installer_oneliner_fetches_and_builds_latest_branch_revision_in_sandbox`: 102 passed, 1 failed, 25 ignored; stderr `../../install.sh: line 121: cargo: command not found`. Exact reproduction of its constructed PATH in the parent shell found `/home/linus/.cargo/bin/cargo` and `cargo 1.97.1`, so the failure is not yet classified as pre-existing; the Bash child environment differs from the direct reproduction and must be captured before any unrelated guidance test change.

This ticket remains incomplete: canonical plan/guidance/lifecycle/parity coverage are still required.

## W10 PTY diagnosis

Shell 2550 was explicitly stopped before any retry (`stop_powershell` confirmed termination). Its apparent 420-second test hang was not a PTY/test failure: the captured log ends in dependency compilation before the test binary was produced. No `install-ctl` child or PTY output existed.

Host/toolchain mismatch is concrete: configured PowerShell builds `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` with Cargo 1.95 / rustc 1.95; `bash` is WSL Linux, where `/mnt/c/...` maps to the checkout and Cargo is `/home/linus/.cargo/bin/cargo` 1.97. The PTY test targets the Windows compiled `C:\Users\linus\git\3\meta-workspace\workflow-tools\target\debug\install-ctl.exe`; it must not use the WSL Cargo/binary path.

A bounded readiness mechanism was added: ratatui-testlib builder timeout 5 seconds, wait for `Artifact categories`, then send Esc and wait for cancellation; either wait panics with captured `screen_contents`. Retrying after 2550 termination again produced no PTY child: at 120 seconds process inspection showed only the configured Cargo 1.95 executable and its `C:\Users\linus\.cargo\bin\cargo.exe` launcher, no rustc and no install-ctl process. The retry was stopped (`stop_powershell` shell 2604), so no indefinite PTY wait occurred. This is an unresolved Cargo build/lock readiness issue before test execution, not a ratatui-testlib protocol failure.

`cargo check --manifest-path workflow-tools\install\install-ctl\Cargo.toml` remains exit 0. Full W10 canonical planner, lifecycle, guidance, and real-install parity work remains incomplete.

## W10 first shared-plan slice validation

Implemented only the approved typed shared installer-plan seam: `InstallOptions` manual defaults and `InstallPlan::from_tokens` reuse the canonical resolver and reject empty selection before apply. Scripted dry-run/apply and TUI review/confirmation now carry the same plan root/options/selection.

Using configured Windows PowerShell Cargo (`C:\Users\linus\.cargo\bin\cargo.exe`), `cargo test --manifest-path install-ctl\Cargo.toml --test plan_regression --no-run` first failed with local extraction diagnostics (orphaned derive and missing resolver import); one local repair was made. The exact `cargo test --manifest-path install-ctl\Cargo.toml --test plan_regression` then passed: 27 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored. This includes the three authored plan assertions and registry catalog freshness.

The nearest attempted selector command `cargo test --manifest-path install-ctl\Cargo.toml selection:: --lib` exited 101 because install-ctl has no library target; no test ran and no retry was made. This is diagnostic only, not acceptance failure.

Lifecycle-aware planning, guidance profiles, literal PTY integration, and real scripted/TUI parity remain later W10 work. Ticket remains on-hold.
